column1: # DRAGON QUEST VII Reimagined, Asian release (0100505021440000): Square Enix / HEXA DRIVE, Unreal Engine 4.27 (IoStore containers beside one pak, PhysX 3.4, MallocBinned3), SDK 19.3.1, NVN,
# CRIWARE sound and Sofdec movies (VP9 through the SDK's movie decoder); update 1.1.0. The JP/WW profile (dm/games/0100A9D01C446000) covers the same engine at 1.2.0: its sdk and subsdk0
# builds are byte-identical, so the SDK patches and the memory layout apply here, and only the main's per-build rows were found again for this build (patches.py, ue_malloc.tsv, fps_locks.tsv).
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie, which Sofdec feeds its VP9 video to)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the game's config caps Unreal at 30 (FrameRateLimit=30, rhi.syncinterval=2), as the JP/WW profile; the host writes t.MaxFPS and rhi.SyncInterval in the
# game's memory (hle_fpslock.c, fps_locks.tsv) to the frame-rate target, so at the Android profile's fixed 30 (android.tsv pacing) the game asks for present interval 2 as on the Switch
# Unreal Engine 4.27: nninitStartup reserves 62 GB of address space unless -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize= caps it, and its FMallocBinned3 cuts 37 GB of pools out of that region; the
# constructor call is cut and the host runs Unreal's heap on a malloc zone outside the guest block (patches.py, hle_uemalloc.c layout UE4_27). The region is 2 GB in a 3.75 GB guest block, with
# the SDK's node-area cut on this sdk build (sdk_patches.py, the same build as the JP/WW profile's)
# the NPDM declares 80 MB of system resource
# A 3D game with a free camera on the right stick: the 3D pad layout. It reads the controller only, so either operation mode works; the player's docked setting decides 1920x1080 or 1280x720
# The shader code archives of pakchunk0-Switch.pak (ShaderArchive-*.ushaderbytecode), each shader LZ4-compressed (uepak.py lz4_shaders): the engine's global shaders and the game's
# material shaders. Unreal combines vertex and pixel shaders per draw from its pipeline state, so every vertex shader is made to link with any pixel shader (shader_split.py separable_pairs)
